validity.recommendation: Do not treat as an independently verified named pipeline. Either find a non-GEM source that actually names the Hilla gas feeder (Arabic Oil Ministry / South Refineries / power-project tenders) or re-scope the row to the real feeder line supplying the Hilla (Babil) gas power station; if none surfaces, flag as an OPEC-table-only stub for possible merge/removal.
validity.researcher_notes: P4062 is a bare stub. Its ONLY citation (both on gem.wiki and in the worklist ref cells, all MISSING_REF) is 'OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin 2017, p.134' — an aggregate statistical bulletin, not a source that names this pipeline. That PDF is no longer retrievable: opec.org now serves a JS/paywall shell (url_verifier: 200 but no 'pipeline' token; direct curl returns an HTML app shell, not the PDF), so the sole support cannot even be confirmed to contain the row, let alone the name. Independent existence search (EN + AR) returns the name 'Trans-Iraq-Hilla-Gas Pipeline' on gem.wiki ONLY — no news, ministry, tender, or trade source uses it. The 25 mi length and 24-in diameter appear nowhere outside GEM and are uncorroborated. The gem.wiki infobox itself is stub-grade: no endpoints (start=end='Iraq'), no operator, no capacity, no start year, and the page categories are still the unedited template placeholders 'Existing pipelines in Country B' / 'Proposed pipelines in Country A'. What IS independently real is the destination and the program: the Hilla (Babil) gas-fired power station exists (power-technology.com profile) and was converted from HFO to natural gas (modernpowersystems.com lists Hilla, Diwaniyah, Samawa among plants switched to gas), and Iraq's national gas network is documented as reaching power stations at Hilla and Najaf (rawabetcenter.com). So a physical gas feeder to the Hilla plant plausibly exists — but the GEM entity as named and specified is not independently attested. Note also MEED describes 'trans-Iraq' only as a PLANNED future LPG line and two future dry-gas lines, not an operating 25-mi gas line, so the 'Trans-Iraq' label may be a mis-derived name.

validity.recommendation: Compare P4062 against P1847 'Strategic-Hilla Gas Pipeline' as a likely duplicate/relabel of the same physical gas feeder to Hilla; also review the whole Strategic-*/Trans-Iraqi-* parallel-naming split (e.g. Najaf: P1848 Strategic-Najaf vs P4064 Trans-Iraqi-Najaf PWR St) as two imports of one central gas-to-power network before keeping both.
validity.researcher_notes: The Iraq gas operating roster contains a SECOND gas line to Hilla: P1847 'Strategic-Hilla Gas Pipeline' (len 72 mi, dia 16 in, cap 0.70, updated 2023-09-09). P4062 (len 25 mi, dia 24 in, updated 2022-07-25) is a strong duplicate/relabel candidate for the same physical feeder. The pattern is systematic: there is a 'Strategic-<city>' family (P1846 Kabesa Cement, P1847 Hilla, P1848 Najaf) and a 'Trans-Iraq(i)-<city>' family (P4062 Hilla, P4064 Najaf PWR St, P4065 Dewania, P4066 Daura, P1852 Nasriyaha) that target the SAME destination cities/power stations — two overlapping labelings of Iraq's central dry-gas-to-power-station network, imported in different batches. Specs differ (72/16 vs 25/24), so I cannot assert an exact duplicate, but the overlap is enough to require a merge review naming P1847. Classification itself is fine: this is a gas transmission/lateral to a power station (in scope), not one of the GulfPub crude/NGL lines — GulfPub has no Iraq gas coverage, so no cross-commodity misclassification.

fills.researcher_notes: Capacity is blank and no independent source gives a throughput for a Hilla gas feeder. Not fillable. Length (25 mi) and diameter (24 in) already carry values but remain uncorroborated by any non-GEM source — left as-is, flagged in validity, not 'filled'.

routes.start_name: Unknown tie-in on Iraq's central dry-gas trunk (~40 km / 25 mi from Hilla; inferred, possibly near the Musaiab/Musayyib power-and-industrial complex — NOT confirmed)
routes.end_name: Al-Hillah (Hilla) gas-fired power station, Babil province
routes.corridor_desc: Only the destination is defensible: the line supplies the Hilla gas-fired power plant in Babil province, central Iraq (Al-Hillah city ~32.48N, 44.43E; the gas plant sits just SW of the city on the Hilla-Karbala road). At the GEM length of ~40 km the origin would be a tie-in on Iraq's south-to-Baghdad-to-center national gas trunk; a plausible but UNCONFIRMED origin is the Musaiab/Musayyib hub ~35-40 km north. The start endpoint is not sourced, so the corridor is only loosely bounded to central Babil around Al-Hillah — tightest defensible bound is 'a <~40 km central-Iraq gas lateral terminating at the Hilla power station.'
routes.researcher_notes: End endpoint (Hilla gas power station, Babil) established from two independent sources confirming a gas-fired plant at Hilla that was switched to natural gas, plus the national-network description reaching Hilla. Al-Hillah city coordinates are a well-known geographic fact used for the endpoint; the exact plant location (SW of the city) was not precisely geocoded so a city-center point is used. Start endpoint is genuinely unsourced — lat/lon left null and described in words; Musaiab as a candidate origin is flagged inferred, not asserted. No coordinates were fabricated.

summary: P4062 is an OPEC-2017-table-only stub: name appears on no independent source, specs uncorroborated, and it overlaps P1847 Strategic-Hilla — real destination (Hilla gas power plant) but unverified as a named/specified pipeline.
